history.summary: Shree Bagetil Ganpati Mandir is a Ganesha temple on the Sangli-Haripur road in Haripur village, Miraj taluka, about 4 km from Sangli ST bus stand and 1 km before the Sangameshwar temple. It was installed in 1834 by Shri Chintaman Rao Patwardhan of the Sangli royal family and was regarded as especially pious by the Patwardhans. The temple sits near the bank of the Krishna river amid dense greenery (coconut and mango trees) and is a popular morning and family destination for Sangli residents. Devotees from Sangli and neighbouring areas flock here on Ganesha's birthday.

name: Ganapati Temple (Bagetala Ganpati)
town: Haripur (Miraj taluka; CSV town 'Sangli' is the district HQ, ~4 km away)
town_description: Haripur is a village on the banks of the Krishna river about 4 km from Sangli city, at the confluence of the Krishna and Warna (Varna) rivers. It was developed by the Patwardhans (Govind Hari Patwardhan built houses for Brahmins here in 1768) and is named after Hari Patwardhan. Haripur's riverside temples - Bagetil Ganapati and the Sangameshwar Shiva temple at the sangam - make it Sangli's main pilgrim-and-picnic suburb.

travel.road: On the Sangli-Haripur road, 4 km from Sangli ST bus stand; about 1 km before the Sangameshwar temple (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: Year-round; pleasant in the early morning and during Ganesh Chaturthi.
